description: This topic explains the meaning and types of crop pests, the damage they cause to crops in the field and in storage, and the various methods used to control them safely.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best defines a crop pest?

options.text: Any organism that improves crop yield
Any living organism that damages crops and causes economic loss
A nutrient deficiency in the soil

mcq.explanation: A pest is any living organism that attacks crops and causes damage leading to reduced yield or economic loss.

mcq.questionText: Which group of pests is characterised by having six legs and three body parts?
mcq.explanation: Insects have three body parts (head, thorax and abdomen) and six legs, and are the most common crop pests.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a rodent pest of crops?
mcq.explanation: Rats and mice are rodents that gnaw and feed on crops both in the field and in stores.

mcq.questionText: Quelea birds are most destructive to which type of crop?

options.text: Cereal grains such as rice and sorghum

mcq.explanation: Quelea birds feed on cereal grains like rice, sorghum and millet, often causing heavy losses in large flocks.

mcq.questionText: Nematodes that attack crops are best described as which of the following?
mcq.explanation: Nematodes are microscopic roundworms that mostly attack plant roots, causing galls and poor growth.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a storage pest of grains?
mcq.explanation: Weevils are common storage pests that bore into and destroy stored grains such as maize and beans.

mcq.questionText: A pest that attacks crops while they are still growing in the garden is called a:
mcq.explanation: Field pests attack crops in the field during growth, while storage pests attack harvested produce in stores.

mcq.questionText: Which method of pest control involves using natural enemies such as predators and parasites?
mcq.explanation: Biological control uses living organisms such as predators, parasites and pathogens to reduce pest populations.

mcq.questionText: Crop rotation helps to control pests mainly because it:

options.text: Breaks the life cycle of pests that depend on one crop

mcq.explanation: Rotating crops denies host-specific pests their preferred food, breaking their life cycle and reducing their numbers.

mcq.questionText: Chemicals used specifically to kill insect pests are called:
mcq.explanation: Insecticides are pesticides made to kill insects, while rodenticides kill rodents and herbicides kill weeds.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a mechanical or physical method of pest control?
mcq.explanation: Hand-picking, trapping and using scarecrows are physical or mechanical methods that physically remove or block pests.

mcq.questionText: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) is best described as:

options.text: Combining several control methods to manage pests effectively

mcq.explanation: IPM combines cultural, biological, physical and chemical methods to control pests with minimal harm to the environment.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a recommended safety practice when using pesticides?

options.text: Spraying against the direction of the wind
Wearing protective clothing such as gloves and a mask

mcq.explanation: Protective clothing such as gloves, masks and overalls prevents pesticides from entering the body through skin or breathing.

mcq.questionText: An aphid damages crops mainly by:

options.text: Gnawing the stem with sharp teeth
Sucking sap from leaves and stems

mcq.explanation: Aphids are sucking insects that pierce plant tissue and suck sap, weakening the plant and spreading diseases.

mcq.questionText: Why is it dangerous to use the same chemical pesticide repeatedly on the same pest for many years?

options.text: The pest may develop resistance to the chemical

mcq.explanation: Repeated use of one chemical can cause pests to develop resistance, making the pesticide less effective over time.

fib.questionText: A living organism that damages crops and causes economic loss is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A pest is any organism harmful to crops or stored produce.

fib.questionText: Pests that attack harvested produce kept in stores are known as _____ pests.
fib.explanation: Storage pests, such as weevils, attack grains and other produce after harvest.

fib.questionText: Microscopic roundworms that attack plant roots are called _____.
fib.explanation: Nematodes are tiny worms in the soil that cause galls and poor root growth.

fib.questionText: The method of pest control that uses natural enemies of pests is called _____ control.
fib.explanation: Biological control relies on predators, parasites and pathogens to reduce pest numbers.

fib.questionText: Chemicals used to kill pests are generally called _____.
fib.explanation: Pesticides include insecticides, rodenticides and other chemicals used against pests.

fib.questionText: Growing different crops on the same land in different seasons to break pest life cycles is called crop _____.
fib.explanation: Crop rotation denies host-specific pests a continuous food supply.

fib.questionText: The approach that combines several pest control methods is abbreviated as _____.
fib.explanation: IPM stands for Integrated Pest Management.

fib.questionText: A common storage insect pest that bores into stored maize and beans is the _____.
fib.explanation: Weevils destroy stored grains by boring into and feeding on them.

fib.questionText: When spraying pesticides, one should always spray in the same direction as the _____ to avoid inhaling chemicals.
fib.explanation: Spraying with the wind keeps the chemical drift away from the operator.

fib.questionText: Birds that move in large flocks and destroy cereal grains in East Africa are commonly called _____ birds.
fib.explanation: Quelea birds feed in huge flocks and cause severe losses to cereals such as rice and sorghum.

tf.questionText: A pest is any organism that damages crops and causes economic loss.
tf.explanation: This is the correct definition of a crop pest.

tf.questionText: All insects are pests that harm crops.
tf.explanation: Many insects are useful, for example pollinators like bees and predators like ladybirds.

tf.questionText: Weevils are examples of storage pests.
tf.explanation: Weevils attack and destroy grains kept in stores.

tf.questionText: Biological control involves spraying chemicals on crops.
tf.explanation: Biological control uses living natural enemies, not chemicals; spraying chemicals is chemical control.

tf.questionText: Nematodes mainly attack the roots of plants.
tf.explanation: Most plant-parasitic nematodes feed on roots, forming galls and reducing growth.

tf.questionText: Rats and mice are insect pests of crops.
tf.explanation: Rats and mice are rodents, not insects.

tf.questionText: Integrated Pest Management combines different control methods to manage pests.
tf.explanation: IPM integrates cultural, biological, physical and chemical methods for effective control.

tf.questionText: It is safe to eat or drink while spraying pesticides on crops.
tf.explanation: Eating or drinking while spraying can lead to swallowing harmful chemicals and poisoning.

tf.questionText: Using scarecrows to frighten birds is a physical or mechanical method of pest control.
tf.explanation: Scarecrows physically deter birds, making this a mechanical/physical control method.

tf.questionText: Pests have no effect on the quantity and quality of crop produce.
tf.explanation: Pests reduce both the quantity and quality of produce, lowering yields and market value.

summary.correctAnswer: An organism that damages crops and causes economic loss.
summary.explanation: Pests reduce yield and quality of crops.
These groups attack crops in different ways.

summary.correctAnswer: Pests that attack crops while growing in the field.
summary.explanation: Examples include stalk borers, aphids and cutworms.

summary.correctAnswer: Pests that attack harvested produce in stores.
summary.explanation: Examples include weevils and grain borers.

summary.correctAnswer: Reduced yield, poor quality and spread of diseases.
summary.explanation: Pests lower both quantity and value of produce.

summary.correctAnswer: Using farming practices like crop rotation and field hygiene.
summary.explanation: These practices reduce pest survival and breeding.

summary.correctAnswer: Using natural enemies such as predators and parasites.
summary.explanation: Living organisms reduce pest populations naturally.

summary.correctAnswer: Combining several control methods for effective pest management.
summary.explanation: Minimises cost and harm to the environment.

summary.correctAnswer: Wear protective clothing, follow instructions and spray with the wind.
summary.explanation: Prevents poisoning and protects the environment.

hoq.questionText: A farmer notices that his beans in the field are attacked by aphids, but spraying insecticide every week is expensive and the aphids keep returning. Which approach would BEST manage the problem in the long term?

options.text: Continue spraying the same insecticide more frequently
Use Integrated Pest Management by combining ladybird predators, field hygiene and limited spraying
Abandon the field and plant elsewhere
Stop all control and accept the losses

hoq.explanation: IPM combines biological, cultural and limited chemical control, giving sustainable and cost-effective management while reducing resistance.

hoq.questionText: A store of maize is being destroyed by weevils. Which combination of measures would most effectively reduce the loss?

options.text: Drying the grain well, cleaning the store and applying an approved storage insecticide or dust
Adding more wet grain to the store
Leaving the store doors open for birds
Storing the maize together with infested grain

hoq.explanation: Proper drying, store hygiene and an approved grain protectant together deny weevils suitable conditions and kill existing ones, reducing losses.

hoq.questionText: Why might over-reliance on a single chemical pesticide eventually harm a farmer's pest control efforts?

options.text: It permanently removes all pests forever
Pests may develop resistance and beneficial natural enemies may also be killed
It increases the number of natural predators
It makes pesticides work faster each year

hoq.explanation: Continuous use of one chemical selects for resistant pests and destroys natural enemies, eventually causing worse pest outbreaks.
